title: Sundial field ops — evening scratchpad
content:
Sundial field ops — evening scratchpad

Context / quick summary:
- Onsite: Customer 'Sundial Health' datacenter (edge colo). Goal: finish VPC peering and air-gapped agent install for Private deployment (v1.8.3).
- Day: network prep, baremetal NIC config, jump-host + bastion verification, started agent install but stopped on proxy + KMS access.
- Tonight: capture what we did, sticky notes for tomorrow, and a must-follow checklist for next engineer to resume.

Customer environment notes (important and easy to forget):
- Only outbound via corporate proxy at 10.3.0.1:3128 (explicit auth required). No direct internet egress except to allowed IPs.
- Bastion at 10.12.5.7. Must jump through iptables-jump01 (10.12.5.2) — they use strict host allow lists.
- Management VLAN: 10.12.0.0/20. Service VLANs: 172.31.64.0/18. MTU set to 9000 on infra NICs.
- KMS/HSM: AWS CloudHSM via customer peering (different account). We do not have KMS keys yet; security team must complete key share.
- Hardware: 2x A100 nodes, 1x monitoring node (small), 1x disk archive node. Rack PDUs locked.
- Serial console access: requires physical key; not available remotely. Plan accordingly.

Commands I ran (copy/paste friendly):
- ssh -A ubuntu@bastion.sundial -i ~/.ssh/redwood_field.pem
- ssh ubuntu@10.12.5.7 -J ubuntu@jump.sundial (two-hop)
- sudo ethtool -i ens3; sudo ip link set dev ens3 mtu 9000
- sudo systemctl status redwood-agent || journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200 --no-pager
- docker ps -a | grep redwood || docker images | grep redwood
- kubectl get pods -n redwood --show-labels (cluster is rook-ceph not used for runtime)

Actions completed today:
- Verified network ACLs allowed peering control plane CIDR (10.50.0.0/22) — had to request ingress from ops team.
- Installed base OS packages (python3, jq, docker).
- Deployed redwood-agent binary (v1.8.3) to monitoring node; it starts but fails on KMS handshake.
- Brought up minimal cluster network (flannel) for testing; will be replaced with CNI per prod config tomorrow.
- Recorded hostnames and MAC addresses in spreadsheet (see linked artifact).

Blockers / unresolved items (priority order):
1) KMS key share not provisioned (blocker): security needs to share key ARN with us. Without keys agent cannot persist credentials. Ticket: RED-2143 (linked).
2) HTTP proxy auth: agent bootstrap needs to reach S3 staging URL, but proxy requires NTLM. Current bootstrap script doesn't support NTLM. Workarounds: a) use local proxy with credential injection during install b) pre-download artifacts onto jump host and SCP them.
3) Bastion host SSH allowlist: my jump host IP not whitelisted for one node (10.12.5.23). Ops said they'll add tomorrow morning.
4) MTU mismatch: a node reported PMTU errors when talking to peered control plane. Suspect kernel offload settings.

Quick mitigation notes I left on hosts:
- /etc/environment (on jump host): set http_proxy and https_proxy to http://svc-deploy:xxxxx@10.3.0.1:3128 (TEMP credentials only on jump host, removed post-run).
- /opt/redwood/install-state.txt: wrote 'stalled: kms-missing' with timestamp.

Checklist for tomorrow (do these in order):
- [ ] Confirm security provisioned KMS key (if not, escalate to Ajay).
- [ ] Get proxy NTLM credentials or plan for local artifact cache on jump host.
- [ ] Re-run agent bootstrap with --no-kms flag to test local-only path (verify container start and health endpoint).
- [ ] Validate MTU + offload settings: ethtool -K ens3 gro off gso off tso off; re-test.
- [ ] Have ops whitelist my jump IP for remaining compute nodes.
- [ ] If KMS unavailable, plan for manual key import later and mark node as 'needs-key' in inventory.

Notes to self / install hints:
- When using patched bootstrap (tmp_bootstrap_v3.sh) remember to change S3 staging to internal mirror URL: https://mirror.sundial.internal/redwood/v1.8.3/
- Agent logs: /var/log/redwood/agent.log rotate daily; size 200MB. Use 'tail -n 400' when debugging.
- crontab: /etc/cron.d/redwood-keepalive runs every 5m; sometimes masks first-run failures. Stop it while debugging install.
- Docker: remove old redwood images before re-test: docker rmi $(docker images -q redwood/agent) || true

Customer reminders / soft constraints to record to ticketing system:
- Security team will only approve credentialed connections from named service accounts, not ephemeral tokens.
- They prefer rolling updates with a 10-minute drain per node. Document scheduled maintenance window: Tue 06:00–09:00 PST.
- Compliance needs audit log forwarding to their SIEM; we need to validate log-shipping daemon (rsyslog -> tcp 6514) config.

Estimated remaining effort: ~6–9 hours (if KMS is granted and proxy creds provided). If KMS not granted or proxy remains NTLM-only, this becomes a multi-day task because of engineering changes to bootstrap.

Questions / TODO for follow-up (assignable):
- Can platform team build a small NTLM proxy wrapper for bootstrap? (ask Ethan).
- Can security provide a temporary key share with time-limited access so we can finish smoke tests? (ask Ajay).
- Create a GH PR for a bootstrap flag --artifact-cache to support jump-host caching (I will draft).

Random field comments (notes-to-self style):
- Remember to remove TEMP proxy creds from jump host at end of day.
- Take photo of rack and serial numbers for inventory (phone is OK but upload to secure drop).

End-of-day status: stopped but safe. Agent runs but not registered with control plane. No data exfiltrated and no prod workload impacted. Pick up from 'kms-missing' marker.

Signature: Priya — leaving keys/envars on jump host for morning team, annotate in RED-2143.
